concepts.name: Array Rotation
concepts.description: Rotates an array to the left by k positions using slicing with O(n) time and space complexity.

concepts.name: Array Reversal (Two-pointer technique)
concepts.description: Reverses an array in place using the two-pointer technique with O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.

concepts.name: Maximum Subarray Sum (Kadane's Algorithm)
concepts.description: Finds the maximum sum of any contiguous subarray using dynamic programming principles in O(n) time and O(1) space.

concepts.name: Two-Pointer Pair Search in Sorted Array
concepts.description: Finds a pair of numbers that sum to a target value in a sorted array using the two-pointer technique in O(n) time and O(1) space.

concepts.name: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
concepts.description: Finds the length of the longest substring without repeating characters using a sliding window approach with a hash map in O(n) time.

concepts.name: Palindrome Checking
concepts.description: Checks whether a string reads the same forwards and backwards using a two-pointer approach in O(n) time and O(1) space.

concepts.name: Singly Linked List
concepts.description: A minimal singly linked list implementation supporting head insertion and list printing in O(1) insertion and O(n) traversal.

concepts.name: Linked List Reversal
concepts.description: Reverses a singly linked list in place by iteratively rewiring next pointers in O(n) time and O(1) space.

concepts.name: Linked List Cycle Detection
concepts.description: Uses slow and fast pointers (Floyd's Tortoise and Hare algorithm) to detect a cycle in a linked list in O(n) time and O(1) space.

concepts.name: Merging Sorted Linked Lists
concepts.description: Merges two sorted linked lists into a single sorted list using a dummy node and tail pointer in O(n + m) time and O(1) extra space.

concepts.name: Doubly Linked List
concepts.description: A doubly linked list implementation that supports bidirectional traversal and O(1) tail append operations.

concepts.name: Stack (Array Implementation)
concepts.description: A basic stack implementation using a dynamic array supporting push, pop, peek, and empty checks in O(1) time.

concepts.name: Balanced Parentheses Validation
concepts.description: Validates whether an expression has matching brackets using a stack lookup table in O(n) time and O(n) space.

concepts.name: Postfix Expression Evaluation
concepts.description: Evaluates a postfix (Reverse Polish Notation) mathematical expression using a stack-based operator handler in O(n) time.

concepts.name: Queue (Deque Implementation)
concepts.description: A queue implementation using a Python deque to avoid the O(n) cost of popping from the front of a standard list, providing O(1) enqueue and dequeue operations.

concepts.name: Circular Queue
concepts.description: A ring-buffer style queue with a fixed maximum capacity that performs enqueue and dequeue operations in O(1) time.

concepts.name: Min Stack
concepts.description: A stack data structure that tracks the minimum element alongside normal push/pop operations using an auxiliary stack in O(1) time.

concepts.name: Factorial Recursion
concepts.description: The classic recursive implementation of factorial calculation demonstrating the call stack mechanism in O(n) time and space.

concepts.name: Recursive Fibonacci Sequence
concepts.description: An exponential-time baseline recursive implementation of the Fibonacci sequence useful for contrasting with memoized dynamic programming.

concepts.name: Binary Exponentiation
concepts.description: Computes base raised to the exponent power recursively in O(log n) time by halving the exponent at each step.

concepts.name: Tower of Hanoi
concepts.description: A classic recursive puzzle that prints the sequence of moves to transfer n disks from a source peg to a target peg in O(2^n) time.

concepts.name: Linear Search
concepts.description: Scans every element sequentially to find a target value in an unsorted array, returning the index or -1 in O(n) time.

concepts.name: Binary Search
concepts.description: Finds the position of a target value in a sorted array by repeatedly halving the search interval in O(log n) time, implemented both iteratively and recursively.

concepts.name: Binary Search Range Queries
concepts.description: Finds the starting and ending indices of a target value in a sorted array by performing two modified binary searches in O(log n) time.

concepts.name: Bubble Sort
concepts.description: A simple comparison-based sorting algorithm that repeatedly steps through the list, compares adjacent elements, and swaps them if they are in the wrong order. Time complexity O(n^2), space O(1).

concepts.name: Selection Sort
concepts.description: A comparison sort that selects the minimum remaining element on each pass and swaps it into its correct position. Time complexity O(n^2), space O(1).

concepts.name: Insertion Sort
concepts.description: Builds the sorted array one element at a time by inserting each element into its correct position. Efficient on nearly-sorted data. Time complexity O(n^2) worst, O(n) best, space O(1).

concepts.name: Merge Sort
concepts.description: A divide-and-conquer sorting algorithm that divides the array into halves, recursively sorts them, and merges the sorted halves. Time complexity O(n log n), space O(n).

concepts.name: Quick Sort
concepts.description: An in-place, divide-and-conquer sorting algorithm that partitions the array around a pivot and recursively sorts the sub-arrays. Average time complexity O(n log n), worst-case O(n^2), space O(log n).

concepts.name: Heap Sort
concepts.description: A comparison-based sorting algorithm that builds a max-heap, repeatedly extracts the maximum element, and reconstructs the heap. Time complexity O(n log n), space O(1).

concepts.name: Counting Sort
concepts.description: A non-comparison integer sorting algorithm that counts the occurrences of each value and reconstructs the sorted array. Time complexity O(n + k), space O(k), where k is the range of input.

concepts.name: Hash Table Implementation
concepts.description: A data structure that implements an associative array using a hash function to map keys to indices in an array of buckets (linked lists) to resolve collisions. Average time O(1), space O(n).

concepts.name: Two Sum Problem
concepts.description: An algorithmic problem that finds indices of two numbers adding up to a target, solved efficiently in O(n) time using a hash map to store seen values and their indices.

concepts.name: Group Anagrams Problem
concepts.description: Groups words that are anagrams of each other by using a sorted-key hash map to categorize words based on their sorted character sequence. Time complexity O(n * k log k), space O(n * k).

concepts.name: First Unique Character in a String
concepts.description: Finds the index of the first non-repeating character in a string using a frequency map (Counter) to store character counts. Time complexity O(n), space O(1) for bounded alphabet.

concepts.name: Binary Search Tree (BST) Operations
concepts.description: A tree data structure where each node has at most two children, maintaining the invariant left child < node < right child. Supports search and insert operations in O(h) time, where h is the tree height.

concepts.name: Tree Traversals (Inorder, Preorder, Postorder)
concepts.description: Depth-first search traversal orders for binary trees: inorder (left, root, right), preorder (root, left, right), and postorder (left, right, root). Time complexity O(n), space O(h).

concepts.name: Level-order Traversal (BFS)
concepts.description: A tree traversal that visits nodes level by level from top to bottom, left to right, using a queue. Time complexity O(n), space O(n).

concepts.name: Tree Height/Depth Calculation
concepts.description: Recursively computes the maximum depth/height of a binary tree as 1 plus the maximum of the heights of the left and right subtrees. Time complexity O(n), space O(h).

concepts.name: BST Validation
concepts.description: Checks if a binary tree is a valid Binary Search Tree by verifying that each node's value lies within a valid (min, max) range passed down recursively. Time complexity O(n), space O(h).

concepts.name: Lowest Common Ancestor (LCA) in BST
concepts.description: Finds the lowest common ancestor of two nodes in a BST by utilizing the ordering property to navigate iteratively without extra storage. Time complexity O(h), space O(1).

concepts.name: Python heapq and Min-Heap Operations
concepts.description: Uses Python's heapq module to implement a binary min-heap, supporting push and pop operations in O(log n) time on a plain list.

concepts.name: Kth Largest Element using Heap
concepts.description: Finds the k-th largest element in an array by maintaining a min-heap of size k containing the k largest elements seen so far. Time complexity O(n log k), space O(k).

concepts.name: Merge K Sorted Lists using Heap
concepts.description: Merges k sorted lists efficiently by using a min-heap keyed on the current head of each list to extract the minimum element in O(N log k) time, where N is the total number of elements.

concepts.name: Graph Representation (Adjacency List)
concepts.description: Represents a graph as a map of vertices to a list of adjacent vertices, supporting both directed and undirected edges. Space complexity O(V + E).

concepts.name: Breadth-First Search (BFS)
concepts.description: Explores a graph level by level using a queue, useful for finding shortest paths in unweighted graphs. Time complexity O(V + E), space O(V).

concepts.name: Depth-First Search (DFS)
concepts.description: Explores a graph as far as possible along each branch before backtracking, using recursion or an explicit stack. Time complexity O(V + E), space O(V).

concepts.name: Cycle Detection in Directed Graphs
concepts.description: Detects cycles in a directed graph using DFS with a recursion-stack marker to track nodes in the current path, identifying back edges. Time complexity O(V + E), space O(V).

concepts.name: Topological Sort (Kahn's Algorithm)
concepts.description: Orders vertices of a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) such that for every directed edge u -> v, u comes before v in the ordering, using in-degree counting and a queue. Time complexity O(V + E), space O(V).

concepts.name: Dijkstra's Shortest Path Algorithm
concepts.description: A graph algorithm that finds shortest paths from a source vertex to all others in a graph with non-negative edge weights, using a min-heap for greedy selection. Runs in O((V + E) log V) time with O(V) space.

concepts.name: Connected Components Counting
concepts.description: A graph traversal technique that counts the number of connected components in an undirected graph by performing repeated DFS from unvisited nodes. Runs in O(V + E) time with O(V) space.

concepts.name: Memoization (Top-Down Dynamic Programming)
concepts.description: A top-down DP technique that caches intermediate results to avoid redundant computation, transforming exponential recursive solutions into linear ones. Demonstrated with Fibonacci computation in O(n) time and O(n) space using lru_cache.

concepts.name: Tabulation (Bottom-Up Dynamic Programming)
concepts.description: An iterative DP approach that builds up solutions using rolling variables instead of full arrays, reducing space usage. Demonstrated with Fibonacci in O(n) time and O(1) space.

concepts.name: 0/1 Knapsack Problem
concepts.description: A classic DP problem that selects items to maximize total value without exceeding a given weight capacity, where each item can be taken at most once. Solved with a 2D DP table in O(n * W) time and space.

concepts.name: Longest Common Subsequence (LCS)
concepts.description: A string DP algorithm that finds the length of the longest subsequence common to two strings using a 2D DP table. Runs in O(m * n) time and space.

concepts.name: Longest Increasing Subsequence (LIS)
concepts.description: An efficient O(n log n) algorithm for finding the length of the longest increasing subsequence using binary search on a patience-sorting pile array. Requires O(n) space.

concepts.name: Coin Change Problem
concepts.description: A DP problem that finds the minimum number of coins needed to make a given amount using unlimited coins of given denominations. Runs in O(amount * len(coins)) time with O(amount) space.

concepts.name: Edit Distance (Levenshtein Distance)
concepts.description: A DP algorithm that computes the minimum number of insert, delete, or replace operations required to transform one string into another. Runs in O(m * n) time and space.

concepts.name: Activity Selection (Greedy Interval Scheduling)
concepts.description: A greedy algorithm that selects the maximum number of non-overlapping activities by sorting them by earliest finish time. Runs in O(n log n) time with O(n) space.

concepts.name: Backtracking (Permutation Generation)
concepts.description: A recursive algorithmic technique that generates all permutations of a list by swapping elements and undoing changes, exploring the full solution space. Runs in O(n!) time and O(n) space.

concepts.name: N-Queens Problem
concepts.description: A backtracking problem that places N queens on an N x N chessboard such that no two queens attack each other, using sets to track used columns and diagonals. Runs in O(N!) time and O(N) space.

concepts.name: Subset Generation via Backtracking
concepts.description: A backtracking algorithm that generates all possible subsets (the power set) of a given set, producing 2^n subsets total. Runs in O(2^n) time and O(n) space.

concepts.name: Trie (Prefix Tree)
concepts.description: A tree-based data structure for efficient prefix-based string storage and lookup, supporting insert, search, and prefix matching operations in O(k) time per operation (where k is word length). Commonly used in autocomplete systems.

concepts.name: Union-Find (Disjoint Set Union)
concepts.description: A data structure that efficiently tracks connected components in a graph using path compression and union by rank. Supports near-constant amortized time per operation (O(alpha(n))) and is used in cycle detection and Kruskal's MST algorithm.

concepts.name: Kruskal's Minimum Spanning Tree Algorithm
concepts.description: A greedy algorithm that builds a minimum spanning tree by adding edges in order of increasing weight, skipping any edge that forms a cycle, using Union-Find for cycle detection. Runs in O(E log E) time with O(V) space.
